senses.gloss: m. pl. (γαμικά, τὰ) marriage, nuptial feast (the guests of which are the witnesses of the marriage; v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Marriage);wedding contract. Pesik. Haḥod. p. 52ᵇ; Yalk. Ex. 190 a king married many wives ולא כתב להם לא ג׳ ולא איפטיא but did not order in their behalf a record of the nuptial act or of the date of marriage וכיון שנשא … וכתב לה ג׳ וכ׳ but when he married a woman of noble descent, he had her marriage recorded as we read (Esth. II, 16) &c., v. אִיפַּטְיָא; Pesik. R. s. 15 כתובת גהיקן (read גמ׳).
units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 32">Ex. R. s. 32</cite> <he>שאין ביניהם גמיסקין</he> for there is between them no wedding feast to testify to their alliance.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 47">Ex. R. s. 47</cite> <he>כתב לה גמיסקוס משלו</he> he had a marriage contract written at his own expense; <he>עֲשֵׂה לה ג׳ ולואי וכ׳</he> prepare thou the certificate, and would I could prevail upon myself to lend my signature to it! [Var. in ed. a. Ar. <he>גמיקן</he>, <cite ref="C01032"><he>גמיקון</he></cite>, <cite ref="C01030"><he>גמיסקין</he></cite>, <cite ref="C01030"><he>גמיסקוס</he></cite>, v. Ar. ed. Koh. s. v. <he>גמס</he>, note.—The nouns γαμισκος, γαμισκα, as if from γαμίσκω, are not otherwise recorded in the Greek vocabulary, and seem to be cacophemistic perversions; cmp. <cite ref="C01010"><he>גמומסית</he></cite>.]
